claims.statement: EU Good Distribution Practice guidance requires transport deviations such as temperature excursions or damage to be reported to the distributor and recipient.

EU guidance and Poland's consolidated GDP requirements require temperature-monitoring equipment used in transport containers or vehicles to be regularly maintained and calibrated; the Polish rule specifies at least annual calibration.

Polish GDP rules keep the supplying pharmaceutical entrepreneur responsible for transport conditions, require written controls for vehicles and equipment, require route risk assessment, and require a third-party transport contract to incorporate outsourced-activity requirements.
Established vendors already market reusable pharmaceutical cold-chain containers through rental or leasing models that include return logistics, inspection, refurbishment, and related services.

Incumbents already bundle real-time temperature and location monitoring, alerts, reports, route tracking, risk analytics, and compliant pharmaceutical logistics, directly overlapping the proposed monitoring and analytics layer.

A disclosed reusable-box deployment used roughly 8,000 boxes for more than one million deliveries and emphasized proximity to logistics routes, cleaning, quality checks, and repair, indicating that density and service-center operations are material to performance.

contrary_evidence: GDP compliance remains the authorized distributor's responsibility even when transport is outsourced, so the pool cannot replace the customer's quality system or release decisions.
Peli BioThermal, CSafe, va-Q-tec, and DHL already offer overlapping combinations of reusable assets, reverse logistics, qualification support, telemetry, reports, and supply-chain analytics.
The Swiss Post deployment cited by va-Q-tec used about 8,000 boxes and a nearby service center, suggesting that a small Warsaw pilot may not reproduce mature network economics.

economics.acquisition_route: Wholesaler-quality teams, courier integrations, and laboratory procurement portals with standardized qualification packs
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Operate 1500 container turns per month by year 3 (unvalidated), expand to regional lane pools by year 7 (unvalidated), and support founder equity above PLN 5 million by year 9 (unvalidated)
economics.founder_time: 12-18 hours per week during validation (unvalidated), with cleaning and courier operations contracted
economics.gross_margin_basis: Repeated asset turns and automated reports after cleaning, calibration, and reverse logistics; 38-55% gross margin (unvalidated)
economics.pricing: PLN 90-220 per container trip (unvalidated) plus PLN 1000-4000 per customer per month for lane analytics (unvalidated)
economics.retention_or_repeat: Annual framework agreements (unvalidated) with recurring weekly lanes

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Pool density lowers reverse-logistics cost while lane history improves packaging selection and audit evidence
fingerprint.customer: Authorized pharmaceutical wholesalers, specialty pharmacies, clinical laboratories, and trial logistics providers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Quality-team framework contracts and courier-lane integrations
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Qualified reusable-container rental, calibrated monitoring, reverse logistics, and lane analytics
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Authorized shipper pays per qualified trip and for monthly lane-performance evidence
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A temperature excursion, packaging audit, new recurring lane, or avoidable single-use packaging spend

founder_fit: Sensor analytics and route optimization fit founder skills.
Framework customers provide repeat revenue with limited public selling.
Operational partners can handle physical work.
risks: Qualification failure or missing custody events.
The stated PLN 190000 startup capital requirement is unvalidated.
Customer quality units may reject a shared pool or require lane-specific qualification that limits fungibility.
Integrated global packaging and logistics incumbents may bundle the proposed analytics at little incremental price.
Cleaning, calibration, repair, insurance, logger connectivity, and failed-return costs may erase the assumed margin.

structure.commercial_archetype: Pooled reusable asset rental with compliance evidence and permissioned lane analytics
structure.control_point: Qualified reusable container inventory plus longitudinal, contract-authorized lane-performance records
structure.critical_dependency: Containers, calibration, cleaning, qualification, custody, and data boundaries must satisfy each authorized distributor's GDP quality system

thesis: Own a pool of reusable, lane-qualified transport containers and calibrated loggers rented to authorized pharmaceutical distributors and clinical laboratories. Customer contracts grant narrowly defined rights to non-personal temperature, handling, and lane-performance data, creating evidence for excursion reduction and packaging optimization; the company rents equipment and analytics but does not distribute medicines.
title: ColdTrace Crate Pool
uncertainties: Which recurring Polish lanes have sufficient density for reusable pooling?
Will quality units accept a shared asset pool and derived lane benchmarks?
What lane-specific qualification, cleaning validation, calibration, insurance, and custody evidence will each customer require?
What are observed container loss, damage, reverse-logistics, connectivity, and labor costs in Poland?
Can a startup obtain qualified containers and loggers within PLN 190000 while maintaining enough spares and utilization?
Will customers pay separately for analytics already bundled by packaging and logistics incumbents?
No signed customer, courier, cleaning, calibration, or data-rights commitment has been observed.
